subject.title: Feature: config-level default task notify policy

question: Which public config shape should OpenClaw support for default task notification policy: one global default, a per-runtime map, or no config surface while solving narrower channel visibility issues separately?
rationale: The source gap is real, but adding a config/default surface changes a public compatibility contract and overlaps narrower Discord, Codex, cron, and subagent announce routing decisions.

options.title: Adopt per-runtime defaults
options.body: Add an additive `agents.defaults.tasks.notifyPolicy` map that keeps current defaults when unset and lets ACP, subagent, cron, CLI, and media behavior be configured independently.

options.title: Adopt one global default
options.body: Add a simpler global default while preserving explicit task policies and carve-outs for current silent runtime classes, accepting less granular operator control.

options.title: Defer config surface
options.body: Keep this issue open but solve only the narrower Discord/Codex visibility bugs until maintainers choose a broader task notification policy model.

recommendation.title: Adopt per-runtime defaults
recommendation.body: Add an additive `agents.defaults.tasks.notifyPolicy` map that keeps current defaults when unset and lets ACP, subagent, cron, CLI, and media behavior be configured independently.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely product choice spans public config schema, subagent/ACP task behavior, docs, and compatibility policy, where steipete is the strongest recent history signal.
